subject: general
question: Which foreign ruler invaded India in 1739, leading to the massacre of Delhi and further weakening the Mughal Empire?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nadir Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nadir Shah**, the ruler of Persia (modern-day Iran), invaded India in 1739 during the reign of Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah.
 
• He is infamous for the **massacre of Delhi**, which resulted in significant loss of life and wealth.
 
• Nadir Shah took away immense treasures, including the famous **Koh-i-Noor diamond** and the **Peacock Throne**, which symbolized the Mughal Empire’s grandeur.
 
• The invasion severely weakened the already declining Mughal Empire, accelerating its disintegration and destabilizing the region.
 
• The invasion was driven by his ambition to expand his empire and the lure of India’s wealth, as well as the Mughal Empire's weakened state and internal conflicts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah Suri (Option 1):**

 
 
• Sher Shah Suri was the founder of the Sur Empire in North India and ruled between 1540 and 1545.
 
• He is known for his administrative reforms, including the introduction of the **Rupiya (currency)** and the construction of the **Grand Trunk Road**.
 
• He did not invade India; rather, he was an Indian ruler who defeated the Mughal Emperor Humayun to establish his reign.
 
 
 
• **Ahmad Shah Abdali (Option 2):**
 
 
• Ahmad Shah Abdali, also known as Ahmad Shah Durrani, was the founder of the Durrani Empire in Afghanistan.
 
• He invaded India multiple times between 1748 and 1767, with the most notable invasion being the **Third Battle of Panipat in 1761**, where he defeated the Marathas.
 
• Though he caused significant damage to India, his invasions occurred after Nadir Shah’s invasion.
 
 
 
• **Babur (Option 4):**
 
 
• Babur was the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, ruling from 1526 to 1530.
 
• He invaded India in 1526 and defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the **First Battle of Panipat**, marking the beginning of the Mughal rule in India.
 
• Unlike Nadir Shah, Babur’s invasion was aimed at establishing a new empire rather than looting wealth.
